name: matches a stable dense reference
input: two query rows, three keys, value width two
test:
import numpy as np
Q=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,2.]])
K=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,1.],[-1.,1.]])
V=np.array([[2.,1.],[4.,-1.],[8.,3.]])
s=Q@K.T/np.sqrt(2.)
p=np.exp(s-s.max(axis=1,keepdims=True)); expected=(p/p.sum(axis=1,keepdims=True))@V
out=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,2)
assert isinstance(out,np.ndarray) and out.shape==(2,2)
np.testing.assert_allclose(out,expected,rtol=1e-8,atol=1e-8)

name: tile size does not change attention
input: uneven final tile; tile sizes 1, 2, and larger than keys
test:
import numpy as np
Q=np.array([[1.,2.],[-2.,1.],[0.,0.]])
K=np.array([[2.,0.],[0.,3.],[-1.,-1.]])
V=np.array([[1.],[5.],[9.]])
s=Q@K.T/np.sqrt(2); e=np.exp(s-s.max(axis=1,keepdims=True)); expected=(e/e.sum(axis=1,keepdims=True))@V
for b in (1,2,5):
 out=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,b)
 np.testing.assert_allclose(out,expected,rtol=1e-8,atol=1e-8)

name: large scores remain finite
test:
import numpy as np
Q=np.array([[1000.],[-1000.]])
K=np.array([[1.],[0.],[-1.]])
V=np.array([[7.,2.],[3.,4.],[-5.,6.]])
with np.errstate(over='raise',invalid='raise'):
 out=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,1)
assert np.isfinite(out).all()
np.testing.assert_allclose(out,[[7.,2.],[-5.,6.]],atol=1e-8)
